## Bounded Pages scan correctness repair

Fixes a **potential low-priority false-positive shared-address warning** in `sharedRouterAddresses`. The prior helper treats two deliveries of the **same** router announcement ID at the same one-time address (for example a receipt-state update) as two independent router records. The repair tracks distinct router announcement IDs per address instead. Different router announcements sharing an address continue to warn; public replay entries are ignored.

Normal `placeScanMatch` ordinarily deduplicates repeated notifications before the UI helper, so **no current browser exploit, funds loss or security vulnerability is claimed**. ## Source-pinned bug fix (GP-BUG-10 / CP-02)

The pending `changePassword()` continuation unconditionally repopulated `ctx` after `ProfileSession.lock()`. Its key context could become non-null while its address book was absent, contradicting `isLocked` and the key revocation contract. Source-pinned benign reproduction: audit PR #312, `docs/notes/bugcheck-2026-11-19/details/core-packages.md`.

**Test-first regression** `68c77b7f9f108d54de0dd1592f432bb27603838e` holds the ciphertext write, locks the old session, releases it, and requires that old session to remain locked while explicit fresh unlock with the new password succeeds.

**Minimal fix** `f7bc60a1b704392e70fe5918766f70a4ab53fb78`: capture the starting key context and install the newly derived context only if the same session remains active after persistence. Same revocation guard pattern as `mutate` and import. No changes to persistence, crypto, backups, contracts, custody or deployment.

**Handoff:** `docs/handoffs/VAULT_REKEY_LOCK_20261120.md` (including test and source SHAs).

**Qualification:** The donor's original handoff preceded execution. ## Why

The existing dual-clock idle lock could preserve active key authority while custody was checked, let stale callbacks cross session boundaries, and miss expiration before a resumed input or promise continuation. Retained sole-copy keys also needed a truthful locked recovery state. Independent integration review found two related private-checkpoint cache/lender boundaries that needed the same revocation rules.

## Changes

- Validate one wall/monotonic clock pair per observation; reject rollback, invalid readings and overdue activity before it can reset a deadline.
- Keep activity history across settings changes, reject retired timer/session callbacks, and check focus, visibility, history, page lifecycle and sensitive-operation boundaries.
- Suspend normal secret operations synchronously, invalidate pending guards and wipe owned temporary buffers before awaiting custody. Dispose recoverable keys only for the session that was locked.
- Preserve sole copies for existing encrypted backup/save/verification, clear transient recovery input on subsequent idle periods, and require normal import/unlock to resume ordinary operations.
- Check authority before reusing private checkpoint slots; refuse and wipe a loan when its matched wallet changes during the final deadline check. The v4 derivation, storage format and scan algorithm are unchanged.
- Add 68 clock/lifecycle unit cases, 16 session-revocation cases, four checkpoint regressions and 11 real-application Chromium acceptance cases, with security guidance and translated notices.

Retained recovery is an intentional custody exception: someone controlling the tab can create an encrypted backup and later unlock it. This state does not provide the confidentiality of erased keys or an authenticated locked vault. JavaScript wiping is best effort.

## GP-BUG-01: receipt archive state belongs to the signed receipt

Source: audit [#312](https://github.com/djshellshoxxx/GhostPay/pull/312), COMP-OPEN-01. When a seller archives receipt A, invalidates the invoice binding, and signs a distinct receipt B, A's completed or delayed archive status can incorrectly disable B's Archive button.

### Test-first focused change
- Two committed Vitest component regressions verify distinct valid signatures, A/B archive writer arguments, reset after completed A, and late A completion after B is signed.

## Problem and result

Completes the implementation for QA-01 from #309. Export, verification, import and unlock shared a cancellation controller but retained independent busy flags. A superseded operation correctly ignored its late result, which left its old controls stuck. The first version of this PR fixed export/verification but left unlock sharing state with durable vault writes.

This continuation binds cancellable busy state to the current operation owner and keeps vault save/delete ownership independent. Cancelling an old backup action releases its controls immediately; its late success or failure cannot clear a newer operation. Pending durable writes stay busy through input edits, cancellation, idle lock and session changes.

## Changes

- Derive export/import, verification and unlock busy state from the active controller and operation kind.
- Release completion state only for the controller that still owns it.
- Give vault save/delete a separate synchronous token; block duplicate writes and preserve their lifetime.
- Include the recoverability preflight in unlock ownership so a delayed check cannot revive a cancelled unlock.
- Recheck export ownership/session after authorization before starting encryption.
- Preserve the generation semantics required for an import/unlock to acknowledge its own session installation.
- Add 17 component regressions and two delayed-operation browser journeys.

## Problem
SellerKeys shared one busy flag between cancellable vault unlock and independent durable vault save/delete operations. Superseding an unlock could leave its controls disabled. Conversely, editing the unlock passphrase or replacing the seller session could enable another vault action while the previous write was still pending.

## Changes
- Preserve PR #314's export/import and verification supersession repair and its ancestry.
- Track unlock and durable-write busy state separately; their union still disables conflicting vault actions.
- Release only unlock state during cancellation, edits or session replacement. A save/delete retains ownership until its own completion.
- Show Cancel vault unlock only for a pending unlock.
- Add three controlled component regressions without changing cryptographic, session-version, reauthentication or storage-transaction guards.

## Validation and review
- Baseline PR #314 source with the new regressions: **3 failed, 2 passed** at the expected busy-state assertions.
- Repaired focused operation suite: **5 passed** using the original Vitest/Vite configuration and one worker.
- All web library dependencies rebuilt serially from the tested worktree's source; installed dependency lock matched the branch exactly.
- Fresh independent source review found no introduced blocker. The reviewer did not independently execute tests.
- Broader SellerKeys selection: **6 files passed, 54 tests passed, one worker error**. The worker running the large SellerKeys.test.tsx was terminated by SIGKILL; the entire selection is not reported as passed.
- Scoped typed ESLint exhausted its imposed 512 MiB heap (exit 134), so no completed lint result is claimed. Full web typecheck/build/browser checks for this repair remain hosted CI gates. No gate or threshold was weakened.

## Problem
The initial tag-scope fix in #317 failed lint and two web regressions: a test expected replacement-seller tags without a fresh unlock, and remounting `Tags` on seller-key changes discarded the existing L1-04 pending-unlock error.

## Changes
- Scope the tag component by chain, so chain changes immediately discard the previous chain's displayed rows.

## Problem
`simulateCall(..., expectBool=true)` treated arbitrary even-length hex RPC replies as `ok`, except a canonical 32-byte zero word. A non-ABI one-byte 0x01, 0x1234 and a canonical-width integer 2 all produced false-positive successful dry-run classification.

## Problem

A CRC-valid multipart QR fragment with a different body for an already held index throws `CHUNK_CONFLICT`, but the assembler refreshed its idle clock before rejecting it. That violates the documented unchanged-state contract and lets rejected input extend an incomplete transfer's lifetime.

The regression accepts part 0 at time 0, rejects a conflict at 90 ms, then supplies the remaining genuine part at 101 ms with a 100 ms idle limit. The original runtime incorrectly completes instead of throwing `SESSION_EXPIRED`.

## Change

Move the activity refresh immediately after conflict validation. Accepted chunks and identical duplicates continue to refresh the deadline; the exact expiry boundary, completion, integrity checks and reset behavior remain unchanged.

Production changes are confined to `packages/qr-exchange/src/assembler.ts`; the other changes are its tests, an additive ownership claim and evidence.

## Problem
PR #276 can report success for two mutable-input races: commit validation rereads different `build-info.json` bytes than those whose hash passed, and an inventoried regular file can be swapped to an external symlink before its path read. Independent review also found that lossy UTF-8 decoding can collapse an unlisted raw filename into a trusted valid Unicode filename, with the same aliasing possible in manifest records.

## Changes
This isolated follow-up is stacked on #276 at `f39a9dd36c09f8b02d937c5f3d19676d334976d6`. The original branch remains read-only.

- Parse the expected commit only from the buffer whose digest matched.
- Validate regular-file descriptor identity and bigint metadata before and after reads, use `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, and close descriptors in `finally`.
- Recheck the inventory and input identities at completion.
- Require lossless UTF-8 decoding of raw directory entries and manifest bytes before matching paths, preserving valid Unicode filenames.
- Retain all six parent test groups and add deterministic regressions and resource/boundary controls.

Exactly four files change: verifier, its test, an additive ownership claim, and a source-pinned handoff. No workflow, dependency, build, contract, application or release-gate change.

## Evidence
Node `v24.22.3`, built-in test runner, 128 MiB heap:
`node --test scripts/pages/verify-pages-artifact.test.mjs`

- Original six plus initial race regressions against unchanged parent: **6 passed / 2 failed / 0 skipped**. Both false-success failures independently reproduced.
- Raw directory-name regression before its guard: **15 passed / 1 failed / 0 skipped**.

The caller must keep the tree, trusted manifest and ancestors private and stable through verification and use. Release notes

Sourced from viem's releases.

viem@2.57.19

Patch Changes

  • #5498 e87e3ec03457c503377648548628180881974035 Thanks @​jxom! - Fixed the Tempo verifyHash hook accepting a signature of a root key that a config commitment retired, which made verifyHash, verifyMessage, and verifySiweMessage read the account's config commitment for a signature that recovers to the account, in every mode.

  • #5496 a0ddd34678563d1bab367357eae5d4ab4553115f Thanks @​jxom! - Fixed Relay.create(...).fetch never answering 413 for a body over 16 MiB when the request had an unread clone.

  • #5498 e87e3ec03457c503377648548628180881974035 Thanks @​jxom! - Fixed Actions.accounts.getConfigCommitment in viem/tempo rejecting on chains without the configurable account precompile, where it now returns the zero commitment.

  • #5494 0fee300f54aa6da04e4d2094c5f169ae1909fd1f Thanks @​mortezashojaei! - Fixed InvalidDomainError and InvalidPrimaryTypeError to set their name, and corrected TxHashNotFoundInLogsErrorType to describe TxHashNotFoundInLogsError.

  • #5490 1e117b1a6cf13fb0fb06ac6e002759fc0a66570b Thanks @​fmrmf! - Added Kinetiq Elysium and Kinetiq Elysium Testnet chains.

  • #5495 f3fe670de4c8df551462602291caf28ff8f5dfb1 Thanks @​jxom! - Resolved the actions called by deployContract, getDelegation, sendCalls, and signAuthorization through getAction, so overrides of those actions on the client are used.

  • #5493 cd91b17b229be5c06c02c57cb80a6188cf10fd0d Thanks @​mortezashojaei! - Appended the generic ErrorType to GetFeeHistoryErrorType, GetEnsTextErrorType, and PrepareTransactionRequestErrorType so unexpected throw sites are assignable.

  • #5488 5c6a920eb5ce88d50f64e22f1d848b29818c48d7 Thanks @​brendanjryan! - Added chainId to ResolvedToken, so a token resolved with token(chainId) records the chain it was resolved for, and added the Tempo Moderato address to ousd.

viem@2.57.18

Patch Changes

  • #5483 78060dbbe684b75fbce8e150adf25fe96145b92e Thanks @​jxom! - Limited the total size of bytes and string values that decodeAbiParameters decodes to 32 times the input size, throwing AbiDecodingSizeLimitExceededError beyond it.

  • #5463 41c1a5f7c7e18560f93d8dd6b251da46f4e1cb5d Thanks @​jxom! - Fixed accessKey.authorize and accessKey.authorizeSync falling back to the client account when account was null; they now throw account is required. instead.

  • #5465 f2c54e49ee6b5665b6b7d9df98149ec1a3c63431 Thanks @​jxom! - Updated batched call to reject every call in a multicall batch when the number of returned results did not match the number of calls.

  • 37a88da74836cb42f82d19ca93a8c873f29fa9b5 Thanks @​ampagent! - Fixed batched multicall, call, and HTTP requests hanging with an unhandled rejection when the batch function threw synchronously, such as an extended readContract action.

  • #5479 ccd175704841433e6ba52af0a53a5a7850619220 Thanks @​jxom! - ccip: Limited the total response size of local batch gateway requests in one CCIP-Read lookup to 10 MiB, failing the lookup when it is exceeded.

  • #5461 55763b62de2eeb3435d18050cbfc9a190c0c74cb Thanks @​jxom! - Fixed call running CCIP-Read callbacks at the default block instead of the blockNumber, blockTag, or blockHash passed to it.

  • #5457 b3af075de8797c707ef028ee3507582430e27023 Thanks @​jxom! - Updated the Celo serializeTransaction to serialize any transaction with a feeCurrency as a CIP-64 transaction.

  • #5474 429c3fce93bb38a12ec0fc8e5bedfe31bf57dce7 Thanks @​jxom! - Fixed getChainContractAddress returning a contract address at block 0n when the contract was created at a later block.

  • #5472 9f0e002f9c81435f74f63858732bf1cf67b49440 Thanks @​jxom! - Fixed Actions.earn.deployErc4626StackSync falling back to the client account when account was null, so it now throws AccountNotFoundError like the other Earn deployment actions.

  • #5476 272622faf010afc39a3369cf2c900a38feea0a46 Thanks @​jxom! - Fixed Tempo Earn deposit, depositShares, redeem, and withdrawExact to throw AccountNotFoundError when account is null and no recipient is given, instead of defaulting the recipient to the client account.

  • #5458 6a08be9a4b1c3888315b395a89060c15b6fc00c4 Thanks @​jxom! - ens: Applied a 10 second timeout to ENS avatar metadata and image requests, and a 10 MiB limit to avatar metadata response bodies.

  • #5468 0231beb3f1048a14d7a93b8e6c88aa16ebcaea9c Thanks @​jxom! - Updated verifyHash, verifyMessage, verifyTypedData, and verifySiweMessage to return false for the zero address and for signatures whose ECDSA recovery fails instead of matching the zero address.

  • #5484 ed3350460ee9327c9c6ec977c578e9c44a984366 Thanks @​jxom! - Fixed Relay.feePayer to reject fills whose requested and filled senders differ, and to validate and sign for the same sender.

  • #5480 a9ec1633f533807bba685812c5cf9fcc0c170297 Thanks @​jxom! - Changed prepareTransactionRequest to keep the chainId argument or chain id over the eth_fillTransaction result and throw ChainMismatchError when they differ.

Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.64.1 to 1.65.1
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.65.1

Bug Fixes

  • #43936 [Regression]: decorated class with a static field fails to load in 1.65 ("_initClass is not a function") with useDefineForClassFields: false
  • #43934 [Bug]: Test locations are one column off under Bun 1.4.4+

Browser Versions

  • Chromium 159.0.8154.6
  • Mozilla Firefox 159.0
  • WebKit 27.2

v1.65.0

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

## Problem

PR #219 established local Bitcoin spend matching, but incomplete and legacy histories could still be called locally unspent, optional provider consent was not enforced at every worker boundary, and chain/session races could leave obsolete sweep authority.

This feature completion preserves #219's original commit and existing scanning engine while making those evidence and permission boundaries explicit.

## Changes

- Derive coinbase identity and consumed outpoints from committed transaction bytes; reject contradictory Esplora metadata.
- Persist backward-compatible, per-output continuous input coverage. Partial scans, historical gaps and source-mode gaps remain `unknown` and unavailable for sweeping.
- Restore encrypted discoveries, observe later confirmed spends, retain chain anchors even for empty all-spent results, and reconcile discovery/spend/coverage evidence after reorganizations.
- Preserve the earliest canonical spend against later duplicate reports; reject replay of an already-confirmed outpoint at a different block.
- Enforce immutable provider consent in the scan API, client, worker protocol and main-thread request bridge. Matched transaction proof requests require light mode; malformed result labels cannot relabel provider evidence as local.
- Keep optional consent revocable during scanning, reject stale session work, and check current scan/live-chain authority before Sign or Broadcast.
- Bound distinct outputs independently of shared tweak buffers; preserve cleanup and existing block, request and checkpoint limits.
- Add deterministic unit, encrypted-resume and full/lean Chromium regressions, reviewed-English security fallback, user documentation and a file-to-acceptance mapping.

Transaction construction and cryptographic signing algorithms are preserved; their spentness preconditions are tightened. The lean Pages profile still excludes Bitcoin.

## Why

PR #234 restored the shared optional pinned-signer parser policy, and #238 already contains its history. Invoice inspection still needed an explicit selected-seller trust policy, confirmed pin management, distinct failure states, and lifecycle guards that invalidate both pending and completed verification.

## Changes

- Add opt-in local seller-name → signing-public-key pins with explicit creation, replacement and removal confirmation, strict storage parsing, cross-tab locking and expected-old-key checks.
- Match the selected seller's exact authenticated key. Another saved seller or a legacy global pin cannot satisfy that selection. A removed selected pin stays unavailable until the expectation is explicitly changed.
- Bind displayed results and payment authority to invoice, selection generation, fresh persisted pin snapshot, session generation and app-lock epoch. Recheck through preparation and final wallet dispatch.
- Distinguish valid pinned, valid unpinned, mismatch, invalid, missing, unsupported, malformed and unavailable results using fixed localized messages.
- Preserve secp256k1 low-s signatures, canonical signing bytes, envelope formats, legacy Settings policy, recovery behavior and security gates. Verification adds no HTTP, analytics or wallet requirement.
- Add eight browser acceptance cases, including an actual idle lock with no seller keys. Correct existing expiry fixtures to cross expiry without also crossing the idle deadline; retain every expiry, wallet and on-chain assertion.
- Keep signer status as a polite live update alongside the existing detailed rejection alert, avoiding competing assertive announcements. No trust or payment guard was loosened.

## Reproduced correctness defect

The exported strict JSON canonicalizer used `Array.map` on untrusted programmatic arrays. Sparse slots were skipped, allowing `new Array(1)` to silently become `[]`, or `[1,,3]` to yield invalid `[1,,3]`. Non-index own properties were silently dropped. The invoice/receipt signing callers currently validate first; no signature bypass, fund-loss exploit, or private-key disclosure is claimed.

## Test-first change

- Exact main base: `14ded337a10c140d7a9f9a9238ec038587d925bb`.

- Full source-pinned limitations and next checks: `docs/handoffs/JSON_CANONICAL_ARRAY_20261119.md`.

The fix validates that array own keys are exactly the indices `0..length-1` plus the intrinsic `length` key before existing recursion. Dense arrays keep their prior canonical bytes. The test rejects holes, enumerable/nonenumerable extra fields and symbols; it retains a nested-dense-array control.

## Why

GhostPay's scan, payment, Sweep, Settings and non-EVM network paths could retain a client or continuation after the user's current choice changed. Malformed private preferences could also degrade into permissive defaults. Esplora, indexer and relayer requests needed independent bounds when fetch or stream cleanup ignored abort.

## What changes

- Add a shared browser authority binding an immutable action, category, selected endpoint, network, operation signal and live settings/session revision. Production unscoped fetch and RPC creation refuse; retries recheck their original grant.
- Refuse malformed privacy records, unknown privacy fields, invalid scan endpoints, revoked permissions and stale settings. Bind cancellation to lock, seller replacement, navigation, input changes and cross-tab storage changes.
- Enforce own-node restrictions through the actual supported adapters, preserve exact URLs or explicit API prefixes, refuse redirects and provider fallback, and keep grants in memory.
- Complete bounded Esplora/indexer/relayer fetch/read/deadline behavior, nonblocking cleanup, late-response disposal and fixed local errors. Preserve #241's EVM/Solana/TRON/startup transport implementations.
- Scope Sweep balance consent to the exact owner/asset and keep quote, send/replacement and status actions separate. Preserve transaction review, signing, locks and ambiguous-attempt journals.
- Protect open Settings forms from overwriting newer endpoints. Stop delayed Pay, scan and policy-lock continuations from reacquiring permission. Require explicit Pay re-review after revocation.

## Problem and scope

The existing TM1–TM15 implementation still allowed unintended endpoint export, stale receipt/invoice disclosure consent, permissive malformed configuration, unsafe CSP artifact acceptance, and additional scan-window requests after cancellation. Actual tight-CSP builds also exposed a mismatch: the policy generator accepted configured origins, but the bundle scanner rejected those origins inside the enforcing policy.

This is a **bounded continuation of #222, stacked on #238** (`198aa5baff22272453733a0f3dcfcac0e0994eec`). It reuses the existing balance consent, session-only reuse ledger, owner checkpoint implementation and shared EVM transport guard. **Draft: required exact-source hosted qualification remains incomplete.**

## Changes and resulting behavior

- **TM4 / TM14:** normalize session-only endpoint retention, offer it for any RPC URL, omit session-only or credential-like endpoints from configuration exports, and reject invalid/incomplete/unacknowledged saved profiles at the existing shared EVM RPC boundary. Copy states the separate scan/indexer/relayer/alternate-chain boundaries.
- **TM5:** validate exact CSP origins and actual early enforcing head-meta/global-header policies; reject unsafe input, inert markup and broadening. Preserve CSP variables through the Pages clean environment and validate its intermediate output. Add matching standard/embed nginx generation.
- **TM5 artifact integration:** accept configured origins only inside validated `connect-src` source tokens in the actual enforcing meta. ## Why this change is needed

Spec 18 already had portable formats and a separate decoder in #213/#229/#238. The remaining gaps could let a download click stand in for a retained backup, let a saved wallet be replaced without fresh consent, or allow stale operations and cached vault state to weaken key-loss safeguards. A final byte-level review also reproduced browser acceptance of a BOM-prefixed file that the strict standalone decoder refused.

## What changes

- Add verification without importing: authenticate the whole encrypted file, validate every recovered key, dispose temporary secret boxes, and return only public metadata.
- Give encrypted exports separate download, user-confirmed retention, and saved-file verification states. Bind verification to the generated file's bytes/text; reject a different valid archive or BOM-normalized file.
- Require fresh replacement consent for every different loaded wallet, including saved wallets. Bind consent to recovered keys, operation and session; recheck vault existence before replacing.
- Cancel obsolete export/recovery results on input, session, lock and lifecycle changes. Freeze captured credentials while busy and preserve the page-close warning when another tab removes the local vault.
- Complete explicit chain constraints, deterministic duplicate metadata and practical secret-buffer cleanup; preserve format/derivation/KDF defaults.
- Extend deterministic component, browser and standalone recovery tests. Complete user guidance and the twenty-threat security review.

Eight findings are resolved (one high, four medium, three low). Review is AI-assisted and independently performed within this workstream; it is not a professional external audit. Supported scope remains ERC-5564 scheme-1 EVM EOAs. No dependency, contract, workflow or custody architecture change.

## Problem

The v4 checkpoint implementation from #235 preserves a cursor after a browser reload while payment observations existed only in React memory. Resuming can skip the completed range and lose the previous discovery from the UI. Slot naming alone also does not authenticate checkpoint contents or prevent concurrent stale writes.

This PR completes the private EVM scan journal for the Pages beta. #235 has now reached main through #242; this PR extends it with v5 persistence and lifecycle protection. It integrates qualified main `e454de6abfefda70d82784fafc1d8949b277c334`, including #241 transport isolation, #237 beta log retention and #242's qualified idle-clock/invoice-signer work. Unrelated unfinished #238 work is not imported.

## Changes

- Commit the safe cursor, original start, bounded public discoveries and incomplete-coverage notes together in an authenticated AES-GCM journal. Private domain-separated v5 slots bind scanning keys, chain, manifest/finality, Deep mode and selected scan configuration.
- Await durable IndexedDB compare-and-swap before reporting a completed page. Random reservations/tombstones reject stale writers, including absence/ABA races and saved-vault deletion. Deleting the single saved seller vault invalidates every v5 context in the profile and reports partial cleanup failures.
- Treat restored observations as claims. Fetch their historical blocks and verify them again before forward scanning; process finality-tail blocks only in the ordinary overlap pass. Incomplete historical replay preserves the previous journal.
- Bound historical replay and forward work separately. Preserve incomplete-coverage warnings and reject a new 1,001st note before commit.
- Guard selected RPC creation, setup, jitter/window dispatch, responses, storage and terminal UI updates. Cancel releases the UI even when an underlying promise does not cooperate.
- Pause private scanning immediately on app-lock notifications, including while recoverability is pending or the sole key copy is deliberately retained. Disable automatic scans synchronously so a due timer cannot reopen work. Preserve seller-key retention and explicit restart.
- Extend Scan status, saved count/height/network and reload/forget recovery; add storage/lifecycle/engine/view/browser regressions and a deterministic journal benchmark; correct companion privacy/troubleshooting documentation.

## Problem and bounded repair

PR #87's major dependency update changes Node socket data typing to string | Buffer. The SOCKS server unconditionally passes a chunk to Buffer.concat, causing TS2345 and a real uncaught runtime error if the socket is configured for decoded text. This repair rejects decoded strings before the binary parser and destroys the connection. The existing Buffer path is unchanged.

Preserves every original #87 commit and all 69 originally changed files byte-for-byte, including its package lock. Merges main 58d89b39b27a66454ebf392bcd35d5c68b57b2f8; only additive ACTIVE_WORK claims conflicted, and both were retained.

The real-socket test configures the accepted socket for UTF-8 decoding. It fails on the old implementation with an uncaught Buffer.concat invalid-argument error. The corrected version requires an actual peer close; timeout rejects instead of being accepted as success.

This qualifies the bounded SOCKS fix only. It does not qualify all of the major dependency upgrades. A minimal root/web compiler compatibility reconciliation is being evaluated separately.

## Why this change is needed

Portable encrypted exports already existed, but users still needed saved-file verification, reliable recovery after a blocked download, and replacement that preserves their current keys when preparation fails. This PR completes Spec 18 for the existing ERC-5564 scheme-1 EVM EOA export path.

## Resulting behavior

- Distinguishes export requested, ciphertext generated, download initiated, user-confirmed retention and verified recoverability. Verification checks the actual saved file, exact generated bytes where applicable, password authentication and key/public identity.
- Provides verify-only recovery without installing a wallet or granting full seller-keystore backup authority. Temporary secret boxes are disposed; cancellation, file selection, passphrase edits and session changes invalidate stale results.
- Retains generated ciphertext after a blocked download so the same file can be retried without another key export or KDF.
- Requires fresh replacement consent bound to the recovered object, operation and session revision. A disappearing vault is rechecked and upgrades the sole-copy warning. Payment, archive, chain, announcement and RPC changes revoke pending export authority.
- Stages all replacement keys before clearing the old session. Partial failure preserves the old usable keys and custody state, disposes staged boxes and wipes owned incoming scalars.
- Cleans owned passphrase buffers on offline input failures, documents all five export formats and proves independent address reconstruction and local spending.
- Preserves the established KDF/cipher, legacy three-key seller keystore, dependency graph, assertions, timeouts, coverage thresholds and release gates. Master recovery restores spending/viewing keys and creates a **new invoice-signing key**.

## Exact sources and integration

This is a draft stacked on #238; #213 and #229 are already incorporated by the selected base.

## Problem

PR #222 validates own-node mode only when constructing an RPC client. AppShell caches clients by chain and URL, while network-profile changes live in storage. A previously created third-party client can therefore continue sending requests after the user selects own node; retries can cross the same boundary.

## Changes

Recheck the current policy at every transport dispatch. Refuse a third-party destination with RPC_URL_REJECTED before sending request data, including reconnects and retries. Keep permitted cached loopback clients usable. Already-sent traffic cannot be recalled. No proxy, OHTTP or Tor profile is newly enabled or certified.

## Summary

Implements the 15 prioritized recommendations in `docs/threat-model/PRIVACY_THREAT_MODEL.md` section 9 (TM1-TM15). Goal: reduce what RPC providers, relayers, website hosts and on-chain observers learn about a seller.

This does **not** make GhostPay anonymous. It remains testnet-only and pre-audit. Several items are opt-in and default off (see below).

## Changes

**Web app**
- TM1: Sweep reads the one-time address balance only on an explicit "Check balance" click, for every user.
- TM2: per-flow provider-exposure notices for Scan, BTC, Solana and TRON.
- TM4: RPC URLs with key-like path or query secrets are flagged; a session-only option keeps them out of localStorage. Existing entries are flagged, never deleted.
- TM5: `apply-csp` postbuild step. `GHOSTPAY_CONNECT_ORIGINS` narrows connect-src in `_headers` and the meta CSP. **Opt-in**: with the variable unset, the broad `https: wss:` default remains.
- TM7: non-blocking warning when a sweep destination was already used in this browser. The record is local only. The known-wallet branch is wired but inactive: no known-wallet list ships yet.
- TM8: checkpoint slots are HMAC-keyed with the viewing key (`v3`). v2 slots migrate without losing checkpoints.
- TM9: receipts omit the one-time address unless the seller opts in. Old receipts still verify.
- TM10: invoices are encrypted by default. Passphrase and opt-out are kept.
- TM12: bulk receipt evidence. **Opt-in** (`bulkEvidence`, default 0). Above the per-page cap, repeated scans of the same range can narrow down which transaction matched; documented in the UI hint.
- TM13: BTC spends are detected from scanned blocks, with a sign-time check against the server. Solana and TRON balances are read only at review time.
- TM14: Tor Browser and own-node profile selection behind a first-use notice. Defaults are unchanged. Everything except `direct` is marked UNVERIFIED.
- TM15: padded scan windows (`padBlocks`, default 0).

**Libraries**
- `chain-adapters`: RPC fetch sends `credentials: omit`, `referrerPolicy: no-referrer`, `cache: no-store` (TM3). Bulk evidence helpers (TM12).
- `invoice-schema`: `stealthAddress` optional in receipts (TM9).
- `scan-source`: `padRange` / `fetchPadded` (TM15). PIR path behind `experimental: true`, default off, PoC only.
- `net-transport`: profile selection (TM14).

**Relayer** (owner-requested; `AGENTS.md` otherwise scopes Pages-only tasks away from relayer changes)
- TM11: optional request padding (`pad` field, 400 `invalid_pad` on bad input), ingress modes (`direct` / `trusted-proxy` / `onion`), zero-log switch.
- TM11 quote-tuple change was assessed and **not** made. Reasons are in `apps/relayer/PRIVACY.md`.

**Docs**: threat model (checkpoint row updated for v3), sweep privacy, Tor (marked untested), BUILD-WEB, relayer PRIVACY.

## Verification (local, on commit `72c4b53`)

- `npm run build:libs`: pass
- `npm run build --workspace @ghostpay/web`: pass, including `apply-csp` and the bundle scan
- `npm test`: web 2795 passed / 13 skipped (coverage thresholds met); chain-adapters 556 passed; invoice-schema 718 passed; scan-source 72 passed; net-transport 156 passed; relayer 480 passed / 5 skipped
- Lint: web, relayer, scan-source, chain-adapters, invoice-schema, net-transport all pass
- `scripts/i18n/check.mjs`: 0 errors (warnings only, for ja/ar fallback text)
- `ci:scan-secrets`, `ci:check-actions`: pass

Not verified: real Tor, OHTTP, own-node or public RPC networks. No CI run had been observed at the time of writing. Treat hosted CI results as the gate.

## Known gaps

- `apply-csp` has been run only against the local production build, not a hosted environment.
- Known-wallet guard for TM7 is inactive (no list shipped).
- `deploy/nginx/security-headers*.conf` keep their own CSP copy; edit `connect-src` there by hand.
- The Pages-only release scope in `AGENTS.md` does not cover this PR's relayer and library changes. Review scope accordingly.

## Problem

Opening Sweep on main automatically queries the Settings RPC for the selected one-time address. Under the existing opt-in path, later application-context changes can also replay an earlier request without another click.

## Changes

Refresh the displayed Sweep balance only from an explicit click. Bind each operation to the selected payment, chain, asset, configured RPC, factory and session; invalidate pending client-creation work and result acceptance on lock, selection changes or unmount. Check before starting the address-bearing lookup after asynchronous client creation and before accepting a result. Existing signing/status RPC paths and already-dispatched transport retries are unchanged. Clear stale balance/quote state. Explain the address, token and connecting-IP exposure without asserting Tor routing. Existing transport retries remain unchanged: one UI invocation is not a guarantee of one HTTP attempt.

This narrow extraction targets main and imports none of #222's destination ledger, network-profile or experimental code. Existing signing, journal and dust-refusal assertions are preserved; browser setup now clicks the consent button.

## Verification

Before repair, regressions failed14/passed2. At runtime/catalog/test source d03d529f5b785dcd129b302d122b191d3d066214, configured focused tests passed120/120; whole-web TypeScript passed with1536MiB heap; scoped ESLint and locale validation passed (4 catalogs,0 errors,415 existing/fallback warnings). Independent reviewer ran72/72 consent+signing tests and found no remaining source blocker. Coordinator reviewed the final runtime diff.

Final local03042f112050966de4616587ad0859f39cba91a6 adds handoff/claim and two independently reviewed+linted browser reentry clicks only. Published tree e003f7d0e2c953d9779c357dabf982069d951ad0 exactly matches that final local tree. Browser suites were adapted but not executed; local Chromium launch is blocked by socket EPERM. Require fresh exact-head hosted CI and browser acceptance before merge. No deployment or release.

## Changes

Keep the advisory reuse ledger in session memory. Delete only its legacy plaintext key, best-effort, without reading or importing those links. Clear history on app lock, seller replacement and silent session clearing. Guard both asynchronous sweep completion paths with captured session/lock identity so old completions cannot restore cleared history. Preserve successful transaction outcomes when cleanup fails. User text explains that prior sessions and other devices are not checked.

## Problem

In #213, a pending recoverability check can outlive the export the user selected. Closing/locking that export and opening another can let the old storage result install the later export, or display an obsolete replacement confirmation.

The export UI also needs two precise disclosures: a private viewing key plus a payment private key and its public announcement can recover the master spending key; encrypted archives retain public authenticated headers that reveal and link their included payment addresses and announcement locators.

## Changes

Bind master-import consent to both its operation controller and selected decrypted export. Add the combined-key authority and archive-metadata disclosures to existing security-critical warnings, the format/recovery guide and offline tool help. Revised warnings retain English fallback in unreviewed locale drafts. No cryptographic format, custody, supported-network or release-policy change.

## Problem

The audit server in PR #224 still exits on a malformed raw request target (`//[`) and serves outside files through in-bundle file/directory symlinks. Filesystem exceptions can also terminate the server. These findings affect the loopback audit helper in docs/audits/poc, not a deployed GhostPay backend.

## Changes

Parse the request URL inside the rejection boundary, require both lexical and canonical path containment, serve regular files only, and read successfully before emitting success headers. Malformed URL/encoding returns 400; outside or unreadable files return 404. A concurrent attacker with write access to served directories remains outside this helper's documented boundary.

## Verification

Before fix: 5 passing and 3 failing test groups. After fix: `node --test docs/audits/poc/static-server.test.mjs` passed 8/8 with zero skips. A separate implementation/review agent and the coordinator independently executed the fixed tests. `git diff --check` passed. Source tree equals locally reviewed ff0e9044fbe7d11bd73e0de56dd9c781e6bc02f2.

Stacked on #224; exact-head CI still required. No claim of SonarCloud resolution: live API reads returned HTTP 403. See docs/handoffs/GHOSTPAY_POC_SERVER_REVIEW_20261118.md.

## Problem

PR #212's proposed disposition checker ignores the production runner's error annotations. Valid-looking JSON followed by a crash/kill exit such as rc=137 can incorrectly return success. The production Mythril runner already rejects this; the flaw is confined to the unwired helper.

## Changes

Reject abnormal exits, clean reports followed by failure, and malformed, duplicate or unassociated error annotations. Retain the ordinary exit-1 path only for a valid nonempty issue report. Document that raw clean reports still lack per-contract provenance and cannot establish complete analysis coverage.

This PR is stacked on #212 and changes only the checker, its tests, claim and handoff. It does not enable dispositions, weaken the Mythril gate, change contracts or authorize a release.

## Verification

Before fix: 11 tests passed, 2 failed. After fix: `node --test scripts/tests/mythril-disposition-check.test.mjs scripts/tests/mythril-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/contract-analysis-workflow.test.mjs` passed 39/39, zero skips. A separate review agent implemented the patch; the coordinator inspected it and independently reran the same 39 tests. This is AI-assisted review, not external security certification.

## Summary

Residual N1 (REVIEW_FINDINGS R-11, #205 SEC-07, #212 SEC-E2-01): the immutable `PolicyAccountFactory` reverts every fee-charging `deploy` when a fee-token view reverts or a transfer moves an unexpected amount. An upgradeable, fee-switch, pausable or blacklisting fee token can therefore freeze the counterfactual funds of every policy that factory creates. `DeployPolicy.s.sol` did not refuse such a configuration, and the README example used it.

- `DeployPolicy` reverts `FeeChargingFactoryNotAcknowledged(feeToken)` when `FLAT_FEE != 0`, unless `FEE_TOKEN_FREEZE_ACK` equals `FEE_TOKEN`. It uses the same EIP-55 parser as every other address variable. `FLAT_FEE=0` needs no acknowledgement.
- `packages/contracts/scripts/pre-deploy-check.sh policy` mirrors the rule.
- The README example now uses `FLAT_FEE=0` (it also gained the required `MAX_FLAT_FEE`). README and `docs/operators/deployment-runbook.md` document the acknowledgement.

This changes the deploy script only. Contract bytecode is unchanged, so the Mythril R4–R11 dispositions stay valid. The owner's N1 decision is untouched: either a zero-fee factory for such tokens, or a specified fail-open `_collectFee`. This makes the fail-closed default mechanical until that decision is made. Nothing is deployed.

Updates `@scure/base` from 1.2.6 to 2.4.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​scure/base's releases.

2.4.0

  • Added base36 coder (lowercase alphanumeric, multibase k payload as used by IPFS/IPNS addresses)
  • Limit base58 and base36 to 2048 bytes due to quadratic complexity. Real-world inputs are less than that.
  • bech32.decodeToBytes / bech32m.decodeToBytes now enforce the 90-char BIP-173 length limit by default (previously unbounded); pass limit: false or a number to override
  • bech32/bech32m: encode rejects non-printable-ASCII prefixes, and decode rejects non-printable-ASCII input instead of letting case folding normalize non-ASCII characters into valid strings
  • base32crockford.decode: non-ASCII input that only becomes valid via case folding is now rejected

Full Changelog: https://github.com/paulmillr/scure-base/compare/2.3.0...2.4.0

2.3.0

  • Massive speed-up of all algorithms. 1 MB speed:
    • base64 encode: 18x, 22mb/s => 395 mb/s
    • base32 encode: 23x, 16mb/s => 367 mb/s
    • base16 encode: 20x, 15mb/s => 294 mb/s
    • bech32 toWords: 8x, 38mb/s => 296 mb/s
    • base58 decode: 8x, 8mb/s => 67.2 mb/s
  • -3.4% reduce of minified bundle size.
  • Reduce on-disk package size: 163kb → 136kb (-27.4kb), by disabling source maps (they became less relevant).
  • Better error messages and stricter type checks
  • Breaking: we've removed internal utils: utils, bytesToString / str, stringToBytes / bytes, and the SomeCoders type. Those were always internal. The coders (base16, base64, …) are unaffected.

  • The privateKey, publicKey, chainCode, identifier, pubKeyHash now return copies instead of live buffers
  • deriveChild no longer blindly try-catches. Use proper filtered-by-kind error handling. Retries will stop at last valid index instead of overflowing with error
  • fromExtendedKey now rejects checksum-valid payloads that are not exactly 78 bytes
  • Stricter HDKey constructor validation: depth must be an integer in 0..255 (throws RangeError), index and parentFingerprint must be valid uint32 values, and chainCode must be exactly 32 bytes
  • derive(path) now rejects paths up front that would exceed the maximum serializable depth of 255
  • Added toPrivateJSON() for explicit private (xpriv + xpub) export; toJSON() currently still includes xpriv for backwards compatibility (planned to become public-only in v3, so migrate to toPrivateJSON() for private round-trips)
  • fromJSON now also accepts { xpub } to restore a public-only key
  • Upgrade deps: noble-hashes, noble-curves and scure-base to 2.4.0.

    • Audited for spec compliance and security
  • Fix all Byte Array types, to ensure proper work in both TypeScript 5.6 & TypeScript 5.9+
    • TS 5.6 has Uint8Array, while TS 5.9+ made it generic Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>
    • This creates incompatibility of code between versions

pull_requests.body:
## Overview
Add a **separate** API-funded GitHub Actions workflow for four independent core-release/QA lanes. Existing `ghostpay-codex-cloud.yml` remains untouched.

- Four concurrent lanes (invoice-schema, recovery browser E2E, script tooling, and localization QA), each constrained to its own directory.
- Two scheduled batches daily, 09:17 and 21:17 UTC, plus manual dispatch.
- One Codex invocation per lane; read-only checkout permissions for development; `:workspace` and `drop-sudo`.
- Two-stage live GitHub open-PR changed-file ownership checks, plus publish-time check; fail closed on overlaps or out-of-lane work.
- Patch artifact handoff to privileged publisher; one separate **draft** PR per lane.
- Integration only after human exact-head approval, current required checks, branch-protection rules, and `--match-head-commit`.
- `$10` per worker per batch **target**, not a hard billed-cost cap. Four workers = `$40` target per batch; twice daily = `$80` target per day, excluding runner fees. Per-lane JSON receipts explicitly record actual cost as unknown.
- Pull-request validation triggers only the non-paying structural test job; no paid agents run for PR validation.

## Verification
Static invariant checks against committed workflow passed. Added `scripts/tests/ghostpay-parallel-workflow.test.mjs` for CI. GitHub-hosted workflow validation and actual funded execution have **not** been demonstrated; this PR remains draft until required checks/review.

## Coordination
PR #47 continues to own the integrated core; this workflow must not duplicate that source. Existing and pending PRs are preserved. No dependency changes, deployments, production transactions, secret edits, releases, or changes to existing automation.

Operating guide: `docs/handoffs/GHOSTPAY_PARALLEL_API_QA_2026-11-03.md`.
